JK42HS40-1704-13A NEMA 17 stepper
Four drive wheels, fifth spare. 0.41 N·m holding, 1.7 A, 240 g each, 5 mm flatted shaft.
Arduino UNO R4 WiFi (from Walleye)
The CNC Shield V3 stacks on the R4's headers; 5 V logic, same pinout. Custom timer-ISR firmware, not GRBL. Frees up when the Walleye rail retires.
TB6600 stepper driver
Spare. No fifth axis in this design.
11.1 V gel-blaster LiPo + its charger

Read the label: mAh, C rating, connector (the pigtails here are Deans T-plug). Needs ≥ 4 A continuous — any C ≥ 4 on 1000 mAh does it. Charge only with a balance charger; if yours is a two-wire wall brick, that is the first thing to replace, not the pack.
USB power bank for the Pi — compact, ≤ 130 g, 5 V ≥ 3 A output

WEIGH IT. A 5,000 mAh bank (~130 g) fits the mass budget only with the drivers at 1.7 A and the fan running; a 10,000–20,000 mAh brick (300–400 g) fails the ramp case at every current. Needs a real 3 A output or the Pi throws undervoltage with the camera and thermal array on. Keeps the Pi isolated from motor-bus noise and from a mis-set buck.
DROK LM2596 adjustable buck converters, pack of 5 (3.2–35 V in, 1.25–34 V out)

One used, set to 6.0 V for the servos (PCA9685 V+); four spare. SET THE VOLTAGE WITH A MULTIMETER BEFORE CONNECTING — these ship at a random output. A second one trimmed to 5.10 V is the fallback Pi supply if the power bank ever drops out.
Three-pin switch
Not wired in until its DC rating is read and is ≥ 10 A. Until then the T-plug is the switch.
Raspberry Pi
Camera, radar processing, servo control, interface. Model still unknown — affects the 5 V budget.

The turret was built for it. Person detection with MobileNet-SSD on the Pi at ~25 fps. If it turns out heavier than 170 g, the ELP board camera (B00KA80N9U, 50 g, $22.49) is the fallback.
